chapter_title: Atmosphere and Climate (Chapter 3, per source PDF's own printed labelling)
subject: Geography (Social Science)
ground_truth_status: Human-verified via second-LLM audit against source PDF text and page footers
expected_concepts: Definition of the atmosphere (blanket of air surrounding Earth, held by gravity, mixture of gases)
Composition of the atmosphere (Nitrogen 78%, Oxygen 21%, Argon, CO2, water vapour, dust)
Five layers of the atmosphere: Troposphere, Stratosphere, Mesosphere, Thermosphere, Exosphere

Functions/features specific to each layer: weather phenomena occur in the troposphere; ozone/UV filtering in the stratosphere; meteors burn up in the mesosphere; radio wave reflection and auroras occur in the thermosphere
Ozone layer (in the stratosphere) filters harmful UV radiation
Weather vs Climate (day-to-day conditions vs long-term average, ~30 years)
Elements of weather/climate: temperature, humidity, precipitation, wind, atmospheric pressure
Insolation and its decrease from equator to poles
Atmospheric pressure: high-pressure vs low-pressure areas, wind flows high to low pressure
Land breeze and sea breeze (local winds)
India's climate classified as tropical monsoon
Four seasons in India per IMD: Winter, Summer/pre-monsoon, Monsoon/rainy, Post-monsoon

Monsoon mechanism: south-west monsoon (June-Sept, sea-to-land, brings most of India's rainfall) and north-east monsoon (Oct-Feb, land-to-sea, generally dry except picks up moisture over Bay of Bengal bringing rainfall to Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and parts of Karnataka)
Climate change: greenhouse gases, causes, and effects (floods, droughts, melting glaciers, sea level rise)
Carbon footprint and ways to reduce it
expected_objectives: Describe the composition and structure of the atmosphere
Explain how the different layers of the atmosphere affect the Earth
Explain the mechanism of monsoon in India

Identify the four main seasons of India per the IMD (Winter, Summer/pre-monsoon, Monsoon, Post-monsoon) as the core, testable classification — the traditional six-season Indian calendar (Ritu) is supplementary enrichment content, not equivalent core material
Explain how human activities contribute to climate change and how carbon footprint can be reduced

known_answer_locations.question: What is the composition of the atmosphere?
What is monsoon and what causes it?
What is the difference between weather and climate?
Which layer of the atmosphere contains the ozone layer and why is it important for flying aeroplanes?

candidate_facts_for_tampering: Nitrogen makes up 78% of the atmosphere (could flip to a wrong %, e.g. 'Oxygen makes up 78%')
The troposphere has an average height of about 12 kilometres (could change the number)
The south-west monsoon occurs June-September; north-east monsoon October-February (could swap the seasons)
Temperature decreases with altitude in the troposphere and mesosphere, but INCREASES in the thermosphere (a good 'inversion' fact to tamper — flip increases/decreases)

case_study_content_not_core_concepts.note: Kept AS a core expected_concept (see list above) since it is one of the chapter's own 'Big Questions' and appears in the 'Before we move on' chapter summary — not purely supplementary.

Treated as separately extractable case-study/application content, NOT included in expected_concepts — it illustrates the monsoon/climate-change concepts rather than introducing a new core concept. If your system extracts this as a real-world application example, that's a bonus, not a requirement.

notes_for_human_verification: Confirm the 5-layer order (Troposphere -> Stratosphere -> Mesosphere -> Thermosphere -> Exosphere) matches what you expect to be tested.
